The only objective is that a page written in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript runs at the same performance as the same screen written by hand in C++. Browser-identical pixels and behavior stay mandatory. A faster path that paints the wrong box, drops a default element style, or skips a test is a failed change.

C++ also repaints, resizes, and handles hover. Those events are required. The generated program does the same work a C++ UI does inside the event, and it does not replay the web pipeline.

- Fixed geometry, colors, text, and images are constants or static tables. Font and image bytes stay in the static arrays from code generation. Startup must not copy them into a `std::vector`.
- A resize runs arithmetic or `LayoutDocument` only because the viewport changed, then paints the new frame.
- A hover that changes color sets the hover node and repaints that control's rectangle from the cached draw records. It does not call `LayoutDocument`, measure text, or raster the whole window.
- A caret blink toggles the cached caret record and repaints that caret rectangle. It does not call `LayoutDocument`.
- A scroll moves the cached frame and paints only the newly exposed band. It does not call `LayoutDocument`. A fixed element keeps a full-frame paint.
- A text edit inside a field, a checkbox, or a radio button rewrites that control's cached records and repaints its rectangle. It does not call `LayoutDocument`.
- A click that opens, hides, or restyles content, a marquee tick, or an animation changes geometry, so a new layout is allowed.
- The first frame copies baked draw constants when the executable was built for that window size. A wider or narrower window stretches those records when the text does not wrap and no length is a percentage of the width. A width that changes line breaks calls `LayoutDocument` once. Returning to a width, height, and geometry already laid out reuses that result. A height-only resize keeps the cached layout when no length depends on the viewport height, and paints only the newly exposed band.
- A click that only marks a link visited recolors that link from the cached records. A click that opens, hides, or restyles boxes calls `LayoutDocument` the first time that geometry appears.
- Unchanged regions are not walked, restyled, or remeasured.

`AdvanceFrame` in `Source/Runtime/FramePlan.h` is the only window refresh path. `LayoutDocument` remains the reference engine for tests and for a viewport or content change. A color hover, a caret blink, and a scroll must increment `dirtyRasterCount` or `fullRasterCount` without incrementing `layoutCount`.

Until the phase that owns a construct is checked, `WarnSlowPaths` must warn that the region stays on the general engine or the interpreter and will not have C++ performance. The page still compiles. Do not silently put a hot path back on `LayoutDocument` or `MiniScript`. When the phase is checked, that warning comes off for the covered construct, and the tests prove the fast path.

Static data is immutable for the life of the process. Dynamic data is recomputed only from the input that changed: window size, hover, focus, caret phase, form value, or a live handler.

The filenames must be PascalCase. The functions, classes, and structs must be PascalCase. Variable names must be camelCase. Constants must be CAPITAL_CASE.

Use the MDN-Reference folder as the reference. Each open goal below names one MDN page or one element. Read that page, implement it, and write a test that matches the browser. After the box is ✅, delete that page's reference file. Use C++ and the Makefile only. Use Python only for a download. The runtime must be independent of the operating system. The renderer must be independent of the operating system. Win32 is a host, not the product.

Give a warning when something will compile but can break behavior. Write tests so behavior and pixels stay browser-identical while the event path stays on the C++ frame plan above. Do not weaken a test, delete a reference check, or mark a slow path as fast to make the build green.

## Progress rule

When a goal is finished, replace its open box with ✅ in this file before the task is reported done. A goal stays open while pixels differ from the browser, a test was weakened, or the event still walks, restyles, or lays out unchanged regions. One goal is one box. Do not check a whole phase while any goal inside it is open. A catalog entry, a parsed attribute, or a warning is not a finished goal.


## Phase 1. Already in the compiler

These boxes are checked because tests already hold them. They are the floor. They are not the MDN behavior goals below.

- ✅ Parse HTML, including recovery, into the document tree.
- ✅ Catalog HTML elements and their default display, margin, and font.
- ✅ Catalog SVG elements and presentation attributes.
- ✅ Parse element attributes and reject attributes that do not apply.
- ✅ Parse style sheets, custom properties, and the CSS properties the validator already accepts.
- ✅ Resolve `<link rel="stylesheet" href>` and `<script src>` from a local path or a web address at compile time.
- ✅ Accept an extra style sheet on `RoboWeb.bat run Page.html Style.css [width] [height]`.
- ✅ Bake the first frame for the window size passed to the compiler.
- ✅ A color hover, caret blink, and scroll leave `layoutCount` unchanged.
- ✅ A text edit, checkbox, radio button, and visited link rewrite cached records.
- ✅ The window paints on launch, and each event blits its dirty rectangle immediately.
- ✅ Compile straight assignments: `document.title`, `textContent`, `innerText`, `hidden`, and `style.color` / `style.background`.

## Phase 13. Performance

The generated program does the same work a hand-written C++ UI does inside the event. These goals stay open while a hot path calls `LayoutDocument`, walks an unchanged record, or emits one draw record per pixel.

- [ ] `AdvanceFrame` is the only window refresh path, and every event above goes through it.
- [ ] A color hover sets the hover node and repaints that control's rectangle from cached records. It does not walk any other record.
- [ ] A caret blink toggles the cached caret record and repaints that caret rectangle.
- [ ] A scroll shifts the cached frame and rasters only the newly exposed band. A fixed element repaints the window.
- [ ] A text edit, checkbox, or radio button rewrites that control's cached records and repaints its rectangle.
- [ ] A visited link recolors from the cached records.
- [ ] A click that opens, hides, or restyles boxes lays out that geometry once. The next click of the same geometry reuses the result.
- [ ] A marquee tick moves cached positions with arithmetic and repaints the marquee band.
- [ ] A CSS or SVG animation samples the cached timeline and repaints the animated rectangle.
- [ ] A wide `filter: blur()`, shadow, and gradient is a fixed handful of records per box, and the pixels still match the browser.
- [ ] Borders, radii, and outlines paint from the cached box.
- [ ] Font and image bytes stay in the static arrays from code generation. Startup does not copy them into a `std::vector`.
- [ ] Returning to a width, height, and geometry already laid out reuses that result.
- [ ] A height-only resize keeps the cached layout when no length depends on viewport height.
- [ ] Remove the `WarnSlowPaths` warning for each construct whose tests hold the fast path.

## Phase 14. Benchmarks

Benchmarks fail the build when a fast event lays out, when a dirty repaint walks the whole draw list, or when the generated page is slower than the hand-written twin by more than the budget. Do not weaken a budget to make the build green.

- [ ] Add a hand-written C++ twin of a fixed screen: boxes, text, one hover color, and a scroll. It paints with the same host blit and no document tree.
- [ ] Add `Source/Tests` timings for 1,000 color hovers, 1,000 caret toggles, and 100 scroll bands. Record `layoutCount`, `dirtyRasterCount`, records visited, and elapsed microseconds.
- [ ] The hover, caret, and scroll timings leave `layoutCount` unchanged.
- [ ] The hover timing visits only the records owned by the hovered control.
- [ ] The generated page for that screen stays within 2× the twin's elapsed time for the same 1,000 hovers and 100 scroll bands.
- [ ] A resize back to a cached size stays within 2× the twin's elapsed time and does not call `LayoutDocument`.
- [ ] A recolor handler compiled from JavaScript stays within 2× the twin's hover time and leaves `layoutCount` unchanged.
- [ ] Record the draw-record count for `Samples\Landing.html` at the launch size. A later change that multiplies that count fails the test unless the new records are required for pixels that were wrong.
- [ ] `Samples\Landing.html` with `Samples\Style.css` matches the browser's boxes and colors at the launch size, and its hover, scroll, and resize stay inside the budgets above.
- [ ] `Samples\Welcome.html` and `Samples\svg.html` meet the same pixel check and the same budgets.

## Phase 15. Cascade and boxes

These rules decide which declaration wins and which box a length is measured against. A property goal in Phase 7 stays open until the value it computes follows this phase.

- [ ] Cascade origins apply in order: user agent, user, author. `!important` reverses that order inside each origin.
- [ ] Specificity and source order pick one declaration when origins tie. A later rule of equal specificity wins.
- [ ] Inheritance, `initial`, `inherit`, `unset`, `revert`, and `revert-layer` match the browser for the properties the page uses.
- [ ] Shorthand properties expand to the longhands MDN lists, and a later longhand overrides one side of the shorthand.
- [ ] Custom properties substitute before the used value is computed, including fallbacks.
- [ ] `@layer` order matches `MDN-Reference/css/reference/at-rules/@layer`.
- [ ] Logical properties map to physical sides from the element's writing mode.
- [ ] The containing block for static, absolute, fixed, and sticky boxes matches the browser.
- [ ] Margin collapse, block formatting contexts, and clearance match the browser.
- [ ] Anonymous block and inline boxes are generated where MDN requires them.
- [ ] Paint order and stacking contexts match the browser, including `z-index` and opacity groups.
- [ ] `box-sizing` changes the used width and height, and percentage lengths use the correct containing-block size.

## Phase 16. Text

- [ ] UTF-8 text, including combining marks and emoji, measures and paints as the browser does with the same font.
- [ ] The `lang` and `dir` attributes and the `bdo` element set the base direction. Bidirectional reordering matches the browser.
- [ ] Line breaking, `white-space`, `word-break`, and `overflow-wrap` match the browser.
- [ ] Font matching walks the requested family, then the generic family, then the built-in face. `@font-face` bytes stay in static arrays.
- [ ] Font weight, style, stretch, variant, and numeric spacing select the face MDN describes.
- [ ] Letter spacing, word spacing, text indent, and tab size change the same advances as the browser.
- [ ] `text-transform` and `text-overflow: ellipsis` match the browser.
- [ ] Ruby (`ruby`, `rt`, `rp`) places annotations the way the MDN pages describe.
- [ ] A soft hyphen and `wbr` create the same break opportunities as the browser.

## Phase 17. Forms, focus, and hit testing

- [ ] `input` types `text`, `search`, `tel`, `url`, `email`, `password`, and `number` edit from cached records and skip `LayoutDocument`.
- [ ] `input` types `checkbox` and `radio` toggle from cached records and skip `LayoutDocument`.
- [ ] `input` types `button`, `submit`, `reset`, `hidden`, `file`, `image`, `color`, `range`, `date`, `time`, `datetime-local`, `month`, and `week` match their MDN pages.
- [ ] `textarea`, `select`, `option`, `optgroup`, `datalist`, `output`, `progress`, and `meter` match their MDN pages.
- [ ] Constraint validation from `MDN-Reference/html/guides/constraint_validation` blocks submit when the browser would, and paints the invalid state.
- [ ] A label focuses its control. Tab order follows `tabindex` and the document order the browser uses.
- [ ] Hit testing returns the topmost painted box. `pointer-events` changes that result.
- [ ] The caret, selection, and clipboard cut, copy, and paste rewrite the focused control's cached records.
- [ ] `contenteditable` edits text inside that element and lays out only when the edit changes line breaks.
- [ ] Disabled and readonly controls ignore edits and paint the disabled face.

## Phase 18. Resources and addresses

Each URI page under `MDN-Reference/uri` is a goal. A relative address resolves against `<base>` and then the page file.

- [ ] `data:` images and fonts decode at compile time into the static tables (`MDN-Reference/uri/reference/schemes/data`).
- [ ] A relative path, an absolute path, and a `://` address resolve the way `MDN-Reference/uri/reference/path` and `authority` describe.
- [ ] A fragment scrolls to that id on load and on a same-page click (`MDN-Reference/uri/reference/fragment`).
- [ ] `srcset`, `sizes`, and `<picture>` choose the candidate the browser chooses for the launch viewport (`MDN-Reference/html/guides/responsive_images`).
- [ ] Quirks mode and standards mode from `MDN-Reference/html/guides/quirks_mode_and_standards_mode` change the boxes the tests name.
- [ ] HTML comments are not painted (`MDN-Reference/html/guides/comments`).
- [ ] An image or font that fails to load paints the broken state and the compile reports the missing resource.
- [ ] A `javascript:` address is compiled with the same compiler as a script and runs on the click (`MDN-Reference/uri/reference/schemes/javascript`).

## Phase 19. Accessibility behavior

Roles that only name an element do not change pixels. Roles and states that change focus, visibility, or the control's value do. The reference is `MDN-Reference/accessibility`.

- [ ] `aria-hidden` and the `hidden` attribute remove the box the way the browser does.
- [ ] Keyboard order follows `MDN-Reference/accessibility/guides/understanding_wcag/keyboard` for links, buttons, and form controls.
- [ ] The accessible name from content, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, and `alt` is the string the window caption shows on hover when the element has no `title`.
- [ ] `role="checkbox"`, `role="radio"`, `role="button"`, `role="textbox"`, and `role="slider"` follow the keyboard behavior on their MDN role pages when the element is focusable.
- [ ] Every role and attribute in Phase 25 is implemented. A role that does not change paint still exposes its name, state, and keyboard behavior from its MDN page.

## Phase 20. Compiler and host

- [ ] A compile error prints the file, line, and column and does not leave a new executable in place of the last good one.
- [ ] Changing only the page rebuilds the generated program and reuses `InterFontData.o` when that source is unchanged.
- [ ] The renderer and layout tests run with no window. Win32 only blits the framebuffer and forwards events into `AdvanceFrame`.
- [ ] Startup of a generated program does not allocate a `std::vector` for font bytes, image bytes, or the baked draw tables.
- [ ] `WarnSlowPaths` names the construct and the phase that still owns it. The warning comes off only when that goal is ✅.

## Phase 21. Memory and startup benchmarks

These fail the build on the same terms as Phase 14. Do not raise a budget to go green.

- [ ] Record the generated process's startup time until the first frame is blitted, and the bytes allocated before the first `AdvanceFrame`.
- [ ] Startup allocations stay at zero `std::vector` copies of font bytes, image bytes, and baked draw tables.
- [ ] A 1,000-hover run does not grow the recorded allocation total after the first frame.
- [ ] A scroll of 100 bands does not allocate a new full-window pixel buffer when the viewport size is unchanged.
- [ ] Compile time for `Samples\Landing.html` is recorded. A later change that more than doubles it fails the test unless the new time is explained by a goal whose pixels were wrong.


## Phase 22. Navigation and the network

The window loads another document the way a browser does, and a script can reach the network while the window is open. A response that only recolors stays on the frame plan. A response that changes boxes lays out that geometry once.

- [ ] Assigning `location`, following an `<a href>` to another local or remote document, and `history.back` / `history.forward` replace the document and paint the new first frame.
- [ ] `fetch` matches `MDN-Reference/api/window/fetch` and runs while the window is open.
- [ ] `XMLHttpRequest` matches its MDN page.
- [ ] `WebSocket` matches `MDN-Reference/api` for that interface and delivers messages without laying out unless the handler changes boxes.
- [ ] `EventSource` matches its MDN page.
- [ ] `Worker`, `SharedWorker`, and `ServiceWorker` match their MDN pages. A message that only recolors stays on the frame plan.
- [ ] `WebGLRenderingContext` and `WebGL2RenderingContext` raster into the canvas bitmap and repaint that canvas rectangle.
- [ ] Each HTTP method under `MDN-Reference/http/reference/methods` is honored by `fetch`.
- [ ] Each status under `MDN-Reference/http/reference/status` sets `response.status` and `response.ok` the way that page describes.

## Phase 23. Scripts that appear at run time

A string that was not in the source is compiled with the same compiler when the call runs, then the generated calls join the frame plan.

- [ ] `eval` of a string built at run time compiles that string and runs it.
- [ ] `new Function` compiles its body the same way.
- [ ] A `javascript:` address compiles its source on the click and runs it.
- [ ] `setTimeout` and `setInterval` string arguments compile the same way. Function arguments call the already compiled function.
